text:
Jamie Benn got his 1,000th NHL point last week, the milestone of a career spent entirely in Dallas, and the Stars have spent the days around it winning. Sunday's 1-0 win over Pittsburgh was their fifth straight, with Jake Oettinger stopping 33 shots for a league-best fifth shutout.

That last part is the key. The Stars are 15-6-2, 8-1-1 in their last ten, and our race model gives them an 88% playoff chance. But over the winning streak they've had only 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), with the goaltending saving 8.5 goals above expected. For the season they've allowed 12.8 fewer goals than their chances predict, and their 32 points sit 6.1 above what their play has earned. Oettinger is the reason: 4.7 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

The skaters are solid rather than dominant, with a 51% share at 5v5. Mikko Rantanen and Wyatt Johnston have anchored the top line, and the Thomas Harley and Nils Lundkvist pair has outscored teams 13-8. Getting Miro Heiskanen back, with an overtime winner against Vegas in his return, adds a lot. The soft spot is finishing: Dallas has scored 7.8 fewer goals than its chances predict.

What to watch: whether the scoring comes back to normal before the save rate does.
headline: Benn reaches 1,000 as Oettinger shuts the door
